# Lembaranz
> A local vault for long-lived secrets — packages v0.2.0

## About
Lembaranz is a local-first, zero-knowledge vault for the credentials that outlive a login: API keys, `.env` files, recovery codes, 2FA seeds, private keys. Data is encrypted locally with AES-GCM 256-bit and Argon2id before storage. No cloud, no tracking, no account required. Runs as a TUI via the `lembaranz` command, with an offline-first web dashboard.

**It is deliberately not a password manager.** It does not autofill, does not sync, and has no team sharing. The positioning rationale, the architectural comparison against Bitwarden / 1Password / Proton Pass, and the expansion path are in `docs/STRATEGY_2026.md`.

## Vault server API

The dashboard talks to `lembaranz server` (`packages/server`), which holds the master key in memory so the browser never receives it. It binds to loopback and requires a bearer token minted per process. The server prints a connect link whose URL fragment carries the origin and token; the dashboard consumes it once and strips it.

| Route | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `GET /health` | Unauthenticated liveness probe |
| `POST /status` | `{ setup, locked }` |
| `POST /recovery-phrase` | Generate a BIP39 phrase, persisting nothing |
| `POST /setup` | Create a vault; refuses with `already_setup` if one exists |
| `POST /unlock` | Master password; wrong password yields `wrong_password` |
| `POST /recover` | 12-word phrase; failure yields `recovery_failed` |
| `GET /notes`, `POST /notes`, `POST /note`, `DELETE /notes` | Entry CRUD |
| `POST /audit` | `{ chain, entries }` — hash-chain verification and recent ledger |
| `POST /stats` | Entry and folder counts |
| `POST /panic-key`, `POST /wipe`, `POST /lock` | Panic key, destroy, lock |

Errors are `{ error, code }` where `code` is one of `wrong_password`, `locked`, `rate_limited`, `recovery_failed`, `already_setup`. Callers branch on `code`, never on the message.

## Project Structure
```
packages/
  core/       — @lembaranz/core      — Encryption engine & storage adapters (atomic writes)
  cli/        — @lembaranz/cli       — TUI (Ink/React) + CLI commands + `server` command
  server/     — @lembaranz/server    — Local vault server (Bun.serve) holding the master key for the web UI
  dashboard/  — @lembaranz/dashboard — Vite + React web client (private/unpublished)
```

### Dashboard design system

One palette, one light source, and system fonts only. The colours and all three
font stacks live in `packages/dashboard/tailwind.config.js`; the shared classes
(`.btn`, `.btn-sand`, `.btn-ghost`, `.eyebrow`, `.chip`, `.glass`,
`.hero-field`, `.paper-field`, `.abyss-field`) live in
`packages/dashboard/src/index.css`. No component contains a literal hex value
and there is no second accent hue. Fonts are system stacks on purpose: the
product makes no network requests, so it must not fetch a webfont from a CDN.
Two rules are enforced by tests rather than by review: every interactive
control must resolve to 44x44px in the compiled cascade
(`touch-targets.test.tsx`), and every class named in the source must actually
compile to a rule (`class-compile.test.ts`, because Tailwind's failure mode is
silent).

`bun run lint:design` (`impeccable detect`) reads source text, so it cannot see
a computed style. Two anti-patterns therefore live in checks that render the
page instead, and both used to ship while that gate was green:

- **No `text-transform: uppercase` anywhere.** `.eyebrow` and `.chip` carry the
  small tracked label look in sentence case. `class-compile.test.ts` reads the
  compiled stylesheet, so it catches the utility both when a component names it
  and when a shared class `@apply`s it.
- **No short label element directly above a heading.** The section label is a
  block span *inside* its `<h2>`, not a `<p>` above it.
  `scripts/verify-render.tsx` walks the rendered markup of every screen with a
  real depth stack and fails on any label whose next sibling is a heading.

A third rule is `contrast.test.tsx`: every run of text must clear WCAG AA
(4.5:1, or 3:1 at 24px) against its own composited background. It resolves
`text-ink/60` and the translucent `.glass` cards to the pixels a browser paints,
and asserts it measured a real page, because a suite that walks nothing reports
nothing and passes. The gradient section grounds are reported separately rather
than failed: the model is position-blind, so it cannot say whether a given label
sits in the lit corner of the hero.

### Build & Run
- Root manifest: `package.json` (Bun workspaces, consolidated dependencies)
- Launch TUI (Dev): `bun run cli`
- Binary name: `lembaranz`
- Dashboard dev server: `bun run --cwd packages/dashboard dev`
- Build verification: `bunx tsc --noEmit --project packages/core/tsconfig.json` and `.../packages/cli/tsconfig.json`

## Core Package Architecture (`packages/core/src/`)

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Vault.ts` | Cryptography engine (AES-GCM 256, key derivation, base64/hex helpers) |
| `Archive.ts` | High-level CRUD for credentials & notes |
| `Context.ts` | Vault path resolution (`personal` / `project` contexts) |
| `Sentinel.ts` | Rate limiting & constant-time compare |
| `Integrity.ts` | SHA-256 integrity hashing |
| `Password.ts` | Master password + BIP39 mnemonic recovery |
| `AuditLog.ts` | Privacy report / audit log (Node-only, browser-guarded) |
| `Audit.ts` | Tamper-evident audit ledger — hash chain, `verifyChain()`, `headHash()` |
| `Senses.ts` | Local content inspection helpers |
| `Formula.ts` | Shared types & `Result<T>` |
| `storage/FileAdapter.ts` | JSON-file storage adapter (atomic writes, Node-only) |
| `storage/BrowserAdapter.ts` | IndexedDB storage adapter (web dashboard) |
| `index.ts` | Public API barrel export |

An exhaustive index of every file and folder in the repository lives at
`docs/REPOSITORY_MAP.md`. Consult it before adding a file, and update it in the
same change.

## Critical AI Rules

### ⚠️ Vault Contexts
Lembaranz uses two main contexts:
1. `personal`: Global vault (`~/.lembaranz/personal.json`, legacy `saku.json`)
2. `project`: Local project vault (`./.lembaranz/project.json`, legacy `pelataran.json`)

### Error Pattern
All async functions return `Result<T>` — never throw:
```typescript
type Result<T> = { data: T; error: null } | { data: null; error: Error };
```

### Security Parameters
- **AES-GCM**: 256-bit key, 12-byte IV.
- **Key derivation**: Argon2id (t=2, m=64 MiB, p=1, 32-byte output) with 16-byte random salts — `Vault.deriveKey`.
  > Legacy compatibility: data created while PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (100 000 iterations) was the active KDF is unlocked through an automatic fallback (`Vault.deriveKeyLegacy`) and re-wrapped with Argon2id; portable backups keep the PBKDF2 fallback for decryption only.
- **Audit ledger**: append-only hash chain over audit entries (SHA-256, `seq` + `prevHash` links); `Audit.verifyChain()` reports the first broken link, `Audit.headHash()` can be anchored externally for truncation coverage. Entries written before the ledger existed are counted as `legacy` and skipped.
- **Storage**: Atomic write-to-temp-then-rename to prevent corruption.
- **File permissions**: vault files `0o600`, vault directories `0o700`.

## Language Policy
- **English is the base language** for code, comments, CLI output, docs, and the landing page.
- **Simplified Chinese (`zh`) is the secondary language** for user-facing UI/docs (`packages/dashboard/src/locales/{en,zh}.json`, README).
- Indonesian identifiers remain only in legacy migration paths (`saku.json`, `pelataran.json`); keep them working, never reintroduce them in new code.

## CLI Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `lembaranz` | Launch TUI (default) |
| `lembaranz setup` | Interactive setup wizard (alias: `init`) |
| `lembaranz launch` | Enter TUI mode |
| `lembaranz browse [keyword]` | Searchable archive browser |
| `lembaranz config` | Configuration manager (alias: `cfg`) |
| `lembaranz doctor` | Diagnostics & health checks |
| `lembaranz dashboard` | Open the web dashboard |
| `lembaranz import` / `export` | Bulk import / encrypted portable backup |
| `lembaranz monitor` | System health & integrity |
| `lembaranz security` | Security dashboard, audits & ledger verification |
| `lembaranz server` | Start the local vault server the web UI connects to (loopback by default) |

### Trust boundary
The web UI does **not** hold the master key. `lembaranz server` holds it in memory and the browser holds only a per-process bearer token, kept in `sessionStorage`. The server binds `127.0.0.1` unless `--host` is passed, answers every route with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and exposes only the vault operations the UI calls.

## Dev Commands

```bash
bun run cli                                           # Run CLI directly
bun run lint                                          # ESLint
bun run test:core                                     # Core test suite
bunx tsc --noEmit --project packages/cli/tsconfig.json   # Type check CLI
bunx tsc --noEmit --project packages/core/tsconfig.json  # Type check Core
```
